concepts.title: Solving Equations with Variables on Both Sides
concepts.definition: When a linear equation carries the variable on both sides, first bring all variable terms to one side and all constants to the other by transposing, then divide by the coefficient to free the variable.
concepts.key_idea: Collect x terms on one side, numbers on the other, then divide.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh102.txt section 2.3 (equations with variables on both sides)

solution_steps.explain: Move every x term to the left and constants to the right.
The constant difference sits on the right side.
Dividing the constant difference by the collected coefficient gives x.

concepts.title: Solving Equations with Brackets
concepts.definition: Equations carrying brackets are simplified by first distributing the multiplier over every term inside the bracket, turning the equation into a plain linear form that is then solved by transposition.
concepts.key_idea: Open the bracket first: multiply each inside term, then solve as usual.
question_patterns: solve the equation containing brackets
find x when 3(2x + 1) = 4x + 11
simplify and solve the bracketed equation
determine x from the given bracketed equation

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the outside factor into each term inside.
Combine x terms and constants on opposite sides.
Transpose and divide to reach the value of x.

concepts.title: Equations Reducible to Linear Form
concepts.definition: Equations that carry the variable in denominators or on both sides of a cross-multiplication can be flattened into linear form: multiply both sides by the common denominator, clear the fractions, and solve the resulting linear equation.
concepts.key_idea: Multiply away the denominators, then solve the plain linear equation.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh102.txt section 2.4 (equations reducible to the linear form)

solution_steps.explain: Clear every denominator so only whole terms remain.
Group x terms on one side, constants on the other.
Divide for x and substitute back to confirm both sides match.

concepts.title: Word Problems with Linear Equations
concepts.definition: Real-life puzzles - consecutive numbers, ages, money shares, perimeter questions - become solvable by declaring the unknown as x, translating every sentence into one linear equation, solving it, and reading off all asked quantities.
concepts.key_idea: Name the unknown x, write one equation from the story, solve, and answer all questions.
question_patterns: the sum of two consecutive multiples of 5 is 55 - find the numbers
a father is three times as old as his son - find their ages from the given condition
divide a sum of money in the given ratio described by the problem
the perimeter of a rectangle relations give an equation - find the sides
Lakshmi is a cashier problem - find the number of notes of each kind
form a linear equation from the story and solve for the unknown

solution_steps.explain: Let x stand for the smallest asked quantity.
Convert the verbal conditions into one linear equation in x.
Solve for x and compute every quantity the question asks.

compute_steps.explain: transpose the terms and divide by the coefficient: x = (87 - 15) / 6 gives 12
